name: gizza-ai/flask-session-sign
summary: Sign Flask session cookies from JSON and a SECRET_KEY.

tool.description: Build a Flask-compatible signed session cookie from a JSON object payload and SECRET_KEY. Defaults match Flask's SecureCookieSessionInterface: salt cookie-session, hmac key derivation, sha1 digest, automatic zlib compression, and cookie name session. Set timestamp for reproducible output, choose sha256/sha512 or alternate itsdangerous derivations for custom apps, and use hex/base64 secret encodings for byte keys. Returns the cookie, Set-Cookie header, serialized payload, signature segments, derived key, timestamp, size, and warnings.

compress.description: Payload compression mode. auto matches itsdangerous: zlib only when it saves more than one byte.

cookie_name.description: Cookie name used in the Set-Cookie header and byte-limit warning. Default session.

digest.description: Digest algorithm for key derivation and HMAC signature. Flask defaults to sha1.

key_derivation.description: itsdangerous key derivation method. Flask configures hmac; itsdangerous' own default is django-concat.

legacy_epoch.description: Encode timestamps as itsdangerous < 1.0 seconds since 2011-01-01 instead of full Unix seconds. Default false.

payload.description: Session data as a JSON object string, for example {"user":1,"admin":true}. Use JSON true/false/null, not Python literals.

salt.description: itsdangerous salt. Flask's SecureCookieSessionInterface uses cookie-session by default.

secret.description: The Flask SECRET_KEY used to sign the session cookie.

secret_encoding.description: How to decode the secret text before signing: utf8 text, hex bytes, or base64 bytes. Default utf8.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp seconds to embed. Use 0 to sign with the current clock; set a fixed value for reproducible cookies.
